rationale: Owner-observed pattern: verification subagents hang forever on compound shell commands (e.g. wl-copy/wl-paste/hyprctl | python3 json.load with no timeout). Wayland clipboard is offer-based (supplier must stay alive); hyprctl IPC can hang; a stdin-consumer (python json.load) then waits forever and the whole tool call never returns. Rule from now on: wrap EVERY external/GUI/IPC command in timeout(1); never pipe an unguarded producer into a stdin consumer; prefer timeout on the producer side so EOF propagates; use wl-copy --foreground under timeout or stage-then-read quickly; keep sleeps minimal; verify restoration with timeout-guarded queries.

Hyprland-like semantics: gaps_in between split siblings at every Split level, gaps_out insets container once.

consequences: Opacity<1 now visibly bleeds wallpaper on Wayland (premultiplied surface). Platforms without PreMultiplied stay opaque + warn. No live-reload caller exists today; configure-time wiring only (Surface::set_opacity available for future reload work).
context: window.opacity 0.5/0.0 rendered identical to 1.0 on Wayland: platform only toggles winit set_transparent(true) (wl_surface opaque region None); no renderer alpha existed (CTX-0261 rerun VERDICT). Options: (a) renderer alpha scaling, (b) documented-unsupported + fail-closed validation.
decision_body: Choose (a): single-pass premultiplied alpha. Surface alpha_mode=PreMultiplied when opacity<1 (chosen only from caps.alpha_modes; Opaque/Auto when 1.0). Fill/glyph fragment shaders emit premultiplied color scaled by opacity uniform; alpha blend pins destination alpha ((Zero,One)) so the buffer keeps uniform alpha=opacity; clear color premultiplied (bg*o,o). Headless compositor scales the finished premultiplied buffer by o for CI-parity tests. o=1.0 leaves the blend equation bit-identical to today.
rationale: Feasible within scope: pipeline already owns fill+glyph WGSL; a uniform + 2 blend-component changes avoid an offscreen texture/second pass and extra VRAM. wgpu 26 requires alpha_mode be selected from SurfaceCapabilities (unsupported non-Auto errors), so configure picks from caps and falls back to opaque with a loud warning (honest + documented). Keeps diff disjoint from CTX-0291 (image blits untouched).

context: Batch review B1 (PX-3585): TerminalCapabilities::allows was wired into four production checks but the only production constructor inserted a single wildcard entry, so allows(t, scope) equalled granted.contains(scope) for every terminal and TerminalCapabilities::grant had no production caller. The intersection mechanism existed but enforced nothing. The reviewer offered two options: wire a real per-terminal grant source, or narrow the issue and evidence to say per-terminal narrowing is deferred. The commander chose the real grant source.
decision_body: A consent-issued automation bearer is the production per-terminal grant. issue_automation_bearer_for_connection records the family terminal scope (Synthesize to terminal.input, Capture and FrameDigest to terminal.inspect) in the issuing session via ControlAuthority::grant_terminal_capability, which clamps the grant to the connection own scopes so a binding can never widen. Semantics: a terminal with an entry is answered by that entry alone (intersection), grants are additive per terminal so family order never traps a client, and an emptied entry is removed so the terminal falls back to the connection wildcard. Revoke, session-end revoke, and expiry release only the capability no other live bearer of the same session still binds. Every failure mode of the mechanism is over-narrow (deny), never over-broad (allow). The ctl control verbs and the debug read surfaces now observe a real narrowing: a read-only binding on t:1 may read t:1, may not drive it, and leaves other terminals untouched. The debug read contract is a coarse debug scope intersected with terminal.inspect (P1-3 resolved by documenting the narrowing rule rather than dropping it).
title: CTX-0780 per-terminal capability grant source: consent-issued automation bearer (issue #1404)

context: Batch review P1-2 (PX-3588): the task replaced the per-connection rate budget with one process-wide RateLimiter shared through Arc Mutex. One abusive client could spend the whole budget and starve every other client, and a lock-poison mapping to Unavailable with no into_inner recovery meant one panic in a connection thread denied all IPC traffic for the process lifetime. The endpoint budget itself is required by issue #1404.
decision_body: Keep both levels. serve_connection_with_shared_limiter checks a fresh per-connection limiter (RC9_CONN_REQ_PER_SEC and RC9_CONN_BURST_PER_SEC, one quarter of the RC-9 values, named in devtools/serve.rs) before the shared endpoint limiter, so one peer can consume at most its share while RC9_MAX_CONNECTIONS peers can still saturate the endpoint bound. A poisoned endpoint lock is recovered with PoisonError::into_inner, matching every other shared lock in the crate; recovery is bounded because the recovered value is a token bucket whose timestamp window is evicted per check.
title: CTX-0780 rate admission is two-level with poison recovery (issue #1404 endpoint budget)

context: bitty #1518: bitty.store.set commits synchronously (atomic temp-then-rename, RC-11 bounded) inside the callback; on slow filesystems the commit alone exceeds the 50 ms RC-1 wall budget, so a cross-VM service call through bounded() and the provider/consumer drive loops failed with the -1 sentinel. CTX-0477 only removed the post-commit E_TIMEOUT inside the writing bridge call.
decision_body: Option A. A thread-local monotonic ledger in bitty-lua records the measured duration of every committed store.set (bridge bounded_store_commit, Ok only). RC-1 wall readings go through BudgetMark, which subtracts ledger growth since the mark, capped at STORE_COMMIT_CREDIT_MAX_MS = 4 x RC1_WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_MS = 200 ms per callback. Applied uniformly: the drive_stashed/drive_chunk loop (own VM and nested provider VM) and the bounded() post-check that guards service_call. Instruction budget untouched; failed writes are charged; time past the cap is charged and suspends at the next slice boundary while the write stays committed. Option B (write-behind) rejected: it changes the documented set-commits-atomically-before-return contract and adds a flush queue and loss window.
title: CTX-0879: credit committed store writes out of the RC-1 wall clock (option A), capped per callback

consequences: Opt-in via JobRegistry::with_job_cgroups; JobRegistry::new keeps Missing(NotConfigured). A fork-before-placement descendant OOM kill is invisible (documented). Race-free placement would need an unsafe-reviewed spawn boundary (clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP), which is out of scope.
context: Issue 1537 needs OomKilled evidence from per-job cgroup memory.events on Linux. bitty-pty forbids unsafe code, so pre_exec and clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP are unavailable; no new FFI crates allowed.
decision_body: Discovery: JobCgroups::discover reads the 0:: line of /proc/self/cgroup (rejecting non-normal components) and the cgroup2 mount point with root / from /proc/self/mountinfo, then tries the own cgroup and its parent as the hosting parent; the host must list memory in cgroup.subtree_control and allow mkdir. A dedicated empty base bitty-jobs-PID-SEQ with +memory hosts leaves job-ID-GENERATION (no-internal-processes rule). JobCgroups::under injects the parent. Placement: the supervisor creates the leaf and reads oom_kill before spawn, then writes the leader pid into cgroup.procs immediately after spawn, before tree adoption and drains. Residual window: descendants forked between exec and that write stay outside the leaf and are not accounted. Cleanup: after reap and tree kill, write cgroup.kill then rmdir with bounded retries; unremovable leaves stay on a bounded list, count against MAX_JOB_CGROUP_LEAVES, and are retried; the base is removed on drop. Evidence: every JobSnapshot carries OomEvidence, with a typed OomEvidenceGap when missing; only an advanced counter plus SIGKILL yields OomKilled.
title: CTX-0880: per-job cgroup v2 leaf placement and delegated-subtree discovery

consequences: On a systemd desktop discover() returns NotDelegated unless bitty runs inside a Delegate=yes unit that has moved its processes into a child cgroup; otherwise the host must configure JobCgroups::under. Live tests need BITTY_TEST_DELEGATED_CGROUP or a delegated namespace root, and skip otherwise.
context: Review PX-4170 found that DEC-0081 discovery adopted the parent cgroup (a systemd-managed app.slice without user.delegate) because mkdir succeeded, which moved job leaders out of the owner scope. It also found that a host-delivered SIGKILL on an OOM-evidenced job was classified OomKilled.
decision_body: Discovery uses only the process own cgroup and only when it is the cgroup-namespace root (0:: path /) or carries the user.delegate or trusted.delegate xattr with value 1, read via rustix::fs::getxattr (safe API; rustix 1.1 fs feature already enabled for bitty-runtime; no new crate or feature). There is no ancestor fallback. The qualifying cgroup must already enable memory in cgroup.subtree_control; the delegator moves its own processes into a child first, and bitty never moves processes it did not spawn. JobCgroups::under is the explicit-configuration path with no marker check. Base creation sweeps stale siblings that are exactly named bitty-jobs-PID-SEQ, whose PID is dead and whose cgroup.events shows populated 0, one rmdir each, bounded by MAX_STALE_BASE_SWEEP. The leaf bound equals the registry capacity. A SIGKILL sent by the host (signal_as Kill, killing cancel, or deadline) classifies as Signaled(9); an advanced counter stays only as OomEvidence::OomKilled. Supersedes the discovery and classification parts of DEC-0081; its placement-window design stands.
title: CTX-0880: per-job cgroup discovery requires explicit delegation; host kills are never OomKilled

context: #1536 needs Win32 Job Object FFI; workspace denies unsafe; only reviewed allowance is bitty-render gpu.rs. Options: (a) new narrow adapter crate with one #[allow(unsafe_code)] ffi module + SAFETY comments + audit update; (b) third-party safe wrapper (none in graph, new ADR-0004 dep); (c) fork portable-pty (ADR-0004 rule 3, heavy). Chosen (a): mirrors rustix/nix role on Unix, reuses locked windows-sys 0.61.2 (MIT/Apache), safe API (JobObject handle type: create kill-on-close job, assign, resume suspended leader, terminate, active count, non-reaping leader exit). Pipe jobs spawn CREATE_SUSPENDED and are resumed only after assignment via OwnedTree::adopt_prepared; ConPTY children (portable-pty hardcodes creation flags) are assigned post-spawn with a documented residual race, follow-up issue. Graceful signals stay typed Unsupported.
title: CTX-0903: Job Object FFI lives in new narrow crate bitty-winjob (windows-sys 0.61, already locked); bitty-pty stays forbid(unsafe_code)

decision_body: Per ADR-0018 and the small-core end state, Beacon POLICY (key language, scopes, menus, themes, provider composition, dispatch of plugin commands) lives in the standalone beacon plugin extension; only the targeting/annotation MECHANISM (TargetEngine/AnnotationEngine, provider registration, label allocation, stale-handle fencing) stays in Core behind the public capability-gated host API. Same pattern for every extraction: policy/interaction moves out, mechanism and security boundary stay. The Wave 4 retirement tasks (W-102 beacon policy, W-103 composer, W-30, W-104 chrome) are what actually remove code from Core; the Wave 2 host tasks (W-28/W-29) only make the mechanism callable by plugins. No standalone plugin work claims Core parity until the retirement tasks land.
title: Beacon end state: policy in the standalone beacon plugin, mechanism in Core

decision_body: Owner steer refining the extraction program. (1) Removal-first: the program deliverable is taking policy OUT of Core into standalone extensions, not growing plugin-flavored APIs inside Core. (2) bitty-plugin-host stays thin: manifest/capability registration, grant/deny, sandbox and loading, generic service/event/command plumbing. It must not accumulate plugin-specific APIs or plugin-behavior tests. (3) Beacon: all policy (key language, scopes/filters, menus, themes, provider choice and composition policy) moves to the standalone beacon plugin extension. Core keeps only the derivation of semantic snapshots from Terminal Truth plus generic provider-registration hooks. (4) W-29 (CTX-0942) is re-scoped to that minimum and must not build a Beacon Lua API surface in Core; its acceptance is unblocked use of generic primitives by an out-of-tree plugin. (5) W-102 (CTX-0928, Beacon policy removal from Core) is the flagship removal task and takes precedence over any further Beacon API work in Core. This refines, not replaces, ADR-0018: the accepted split stands, but the retained Core side is the minimal generic mechanism, and the removal side is now the priority.
title: Removal-first extraction; thin plugin host; W-29 re-scoped to minimum

decision_body: Owner correction superseding the add-API reading of the program. Bitty has an upstream Rust layer and a downstream Lua layer. The Rust layer implements core terminal functionality; anything that is not the terminal itself is an extension (whether implemented as a Rust extension crate/repo or as a Lua plugin). The Lua layer assembles extensions. Consequences: (1) The program work is EXTRACTION — splitting out of Core what does not belong — not adding plugin-flavored host APIs into Core. Prior docs (ADR-0016/0018 retention wording, W-28/W-29 task framing) drew the Core line too generously and must be read with this correction; focused follow-ups will tighten them. (2) bitty-plugin-host and bitty-lua stay thin: registration, capability grant/deny, sandbox/loading, generic plumbing. (3) Code-grounded extraction queue: bitty-runtime/src/execution/* to bitty-execution (W-140); bitty-rich image/kitty decode+place (~7.3k lines) to bitty-graphics (W-141); bitty-ui a11y adapter to bitty-a11y (W-142); bitty-rich composer/shell/hints (~5k lines) out as composer extension (W-103); bitty-ui tab-strip/scratchpad/window-chrome/drag plus bitty-runtime workspace/tabs to bar plugin or retirement (W-104/W-26/W-27); bitty-ui search + search-mode/copy-mode policy to search/copy-mode plugins (W-143/W-144); bitty-package install/resolve/source to bitty-plugin-manager (W-101, in flight); bitty-compat-lab/bitty-perf crates out of the workspace (W-105); Beacon policy to the beacon plugin with only mechanism derivation in Core (W-102). (4) Stays in Core: term-state/vt/pty/render/config/platform/terminal/winjob, selection semantics, bounded search primitive, clipboard permission, thin plugin loading. (5) Open point: the merged W-28 overlay/input-capture mechanism and the W-29 minimal bindings — whether the overlay-presentation half stays in Core or moves to an extension; input-focus arbitration itself is Core-legitimate. No further Core additions until this is resolved.
title: Corrected architecture: Rust upstream implements the terminal; Lua downstream assembles extensions

decision_body: Owner: the end-state crate count (~14-15) is acceptable; the requirement is that everything not belonging to the terminal leaves Core, and that the resulting architecture is well-organized and maintainable. Organization rules: (1) Each remaining crate documents what it owns and what it explicitly does not; no policy hides in mechanism crates. (2) Dependency direction is one-way: extensions depend on Core, never the reverse; no cycles; bitty-terminal (binary) composes everything. (3) Extraction order minimizes breakage: pure moves first (W-105 compat-lab/perf out of workspace), then install/resolve wiring (W-101 follow-up CTX-0944), then the large subsystem extractions (W-140 execution, W-141 graphics, W-103 composer), then chrome retirement (W-104/W-26/W-27), then policy extractions (W-142/W-143/W-144/W-145/W-146). Each extraction is: create the crate in the extension repo with its contract, move code, wire the dependency, delete from Core, prove parity with the moved tests. (4) The four possible consolidations (dissolve bitty-rich remainder, merge winjob, move test-vm, fold test-support) are deferred until after the extractions, decided on evidence of remainder size.
title: End-state organization: ~14-15 crates, extraction completeness over count

decision_body: Owner questions resolved against the bitty-network reference model. (1) Layout: each split-out upstream repo is an independent Cargo workspace using a crates/ layout (a narrow public crate such as *-api or *-wire plus internal crates), matching bitty-network, bitty-ipc, bitty-observability, and the landed bitty-execution/bitty-graphics. (2) Consumption: Core and plugins depend on the NARROW crate they need via pinned git rev (7-char), e.g. bitty-network-wire rev c69fe57 — never a whole-workspace or branch dependency. (3) Optionality: every split-out piece must be something Bitty works fine without; they are upstreams needed by plugin systems, so Core holds zero dependencies on them (one-way: extensions may pin Core crates, never reverse). (4) CodeRabbit suggestions on any repo are adopted where valid (record disposition per PR); reviewer feedback gates merges. (5) Disk: clean worktree target dirs, act artifacts, and /tmp scratch as tasks close; never accumulate .targets/.
title: Extension repo organization: crates layout, narrow-crate pins, one-way deps

consequences: Implementation must pin exact versions, resolve the skrifa range cap, verify swash on 1.85, and run deny plus geiger gates.
context: CTX-0948 needs pure-Rust shaping plus crossfont removal. Candidates were rustybuzz versus harfrust, swash, fontdb, and wholesale cosmic-text adoption.
decision_body: Target stack is harfrust 0.14 plus read-fonts 0.45 for shaping, swash 0.2 scale plus render for rasterization, fontdb 0.23 for discovery. Reject rustybuzz to avoid a second font parser, and reject cosmic-text wholesale because it requires rust 1.89 above MSRV 1.85. Mirror cosmic-text composition with Bitty-owned run shaping.
rationale: harfrust tracks current HarfBuzz, declares rust 1.85, and shares the read-fonts parser with swash and skrifa. All licenses are MIT or Apache-2.0. Full evidence in the design doc.
title: CTX-0948: shape with harfrust, rasterize with swash, discover with fontdb

consequences: Grid gains run formation and cluster to cell mapping. Phase C decides FallbackRasterizer retirement for the grid path.
context: Grid renders per cell through GlyphCache and FallbackRasterizer today. Shaping is run-level, so the per-scalar fallback decorator cannot express it.
decision_body: New shaped.rs module owns fontdb plus harfrust plus swash. ShapedRasterizer implements GlyphRasterizer for single-glyph paths and adds an inherent shape_run method for grid rows with internal fallback-aware shaping. FallbackRasterizer stays only for legacy single-glyph paths during transition.
rationale: Keeps the owned trait seam intact, reuses cache and atlas discipline unchanged, and avoids maintaining two fallback walks long term.
title: CTX-0948: ShapedRasterizer implements GlyphRasterizer with internal fallback

consequences: Config validation, Lua schema, and reload cache-cut land in Phase A. Color emoji and bidi stay explicit non-goals.
context: Issue asks for font.features and font.disable_ligatures. Kitty, ghostty, and wezterm each solve this differently.
decision_body: Add FontConfig features as strict TAG value strings with a 32 entry bound, and a Never Cursor Always ligature policy defaulting to Never. Always forces programming-ligature features off. Cursor reshapes the cursor row from cache.
rationale: Strict wezterm-compatible syntax gives parse errors instead of ghostty silent ignores. Kitty three-state cursor semantics is the proven terminal UX.
title: CTX-0948: kitty-style ligature policy plus wezterm-style feature tags

consequences: Each phase carries acceptance criteria including PB-6 floor verdicts and per-OS discovery evidence.
context: Shaping touches render hot paths budgeted by PB-6 at 40 MB per second, and crossfont removal touches runtime wiring plus deny policy.
decision_body: Deliver in three phases: A stack swap plus config plus removal checklist, B run shaping plus cursor policy, C hardening plus docs sync. disable_ligatures always must restore the unshaped fast path bit for bit and serves as the revert switch. Run-shape caches are bounded LRU with hit and miss counters.
rationale: Phase A stays independently revertable and benchmarked before grid behavior changes. Caches convert shaping from per-frame cost to per-row-entry cost.
title: CTX-0948: three-phase delivery with PB-6 kill switch
